subject: GPU slab sizing + burst playbook — CrownCipher Dedicated
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@crowncipher.ai>, Aaron Li <aaron.li@crowncipher.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU slab sizing + burst playbook — CrownCipher Dedicated

Hi Olivia / Aaron,

Thanks for the time yesterday — good to see the traffic patterns and the three-week spike window you signaled. Attached is an initial sizing workbook (crowncipher_sizing_v1.xlsx) and a short draft playbook for burst/autoscale behavior. High-level notes in this email: 

- Baseline: we recommend a 32-GPU slab (A100-class equivalent) to meet the steady-state request/latency SLAs you shared (95th p99 latency target for prompts).
- Shoulder capacity: add a 50% shoulder slab (16 GPUs) to absorb predictable batch throughput during daily peak windows (09:00–12:00 PST).
- Burst headroom: allow an ephemeral burst pool up to 2x baseline (additional 32 GPUs) for unexpected surges — backed by our transient preemptible slab.
- Billing/credits: we can offer a burst-credit bucket for the first quarter tied to the pilot (see worksheet tab: credit-allocation).
- Autoscale triggers: recommended triggers are (1) sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 2 minutes, (2) queue depth > 120 pending requests for 30s, (3) observed tail-latency breach at 99th for two consecutive windows.

Open questions we flagged for the team:
- Whether CrownCipher is comfortable with preemptible GPUs in the burst pool (we have hot fallback routes to a slightly smaller, non-preemptible model variant).
- Can we get an agreed process for prioritization of inference jobs during burst windows (some models = critical, others = best-effort)?

Next step: If you’re aligned, we’ll draft a short addendum that codifies the burst headroom, credit cadence, and the escalation matrix. Marissa / Ben, could you review the runbook and call out any constraints on eviction windows and canary timeouts?

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0116

Attachments: crowncipher_sizing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 tabs — sizing / credits), burst-runbook-draft.pdf (2-page outline)

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@crowncipher.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU slab sizing + burst playbook — CrownCipher Dedicated

Markus — thanks, this looks useful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Peak window: the three-week event in September is actually heavier at 02:00–06:00 UTC (our users are global). Can the shoulder slab operate on a shifted schedule (i.e., different dayparting)?

2) Preemptible concern: we cannot allow preemption for our inference-critical models that are handling live user interactions. We could tolerate preemptible for nightly batch reranks / reindex jobs.

3) Prioritization: yes, we need a simple policy — recommended order: (A) Live inference (critical), (B) Nearline customer analytics (high), (C) Batch/ML housekeeping (best-effort).

4) Can you sketch the rollback behavior if a burst fails to provision (e.g., fallback to hosted variants or throttled tokens)?

We'd like to get this codified in the pilot addendum — can you include expected failover latencies and cost guardrails?

—Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Platform Engineering, CrownCipher
olivia.park@crowncipher.ai

Looping in some implementation notes — copying the excerpt we discussed internally.

--- internal runbook excerpt ---
1) Eviction & preemption: since Olivia flagged live inference as non-preemptible, we recommend a two-pool model: 
   - Reserved non-preemptible slab (baseline + shoulder) for models tagged "live".
   - Ephemeral preemptible slab for "best-effort" jobs only.
2) Canary windows: staggered canaries with a total warmup of 90s (3 x 30s checks) — if canary fails, do not expand burst further for 10 minutes.
3) Fallback policy: if burst provisioning fails due to capacity, route requests to (a) a slightly smaller model variant that meets latency target for 85% quantile, then (b) degrade non-critical responses (e.g., shorter summaries) as a last resort.
4) Billing guardrail: automatic billing alert at 80% of burst-credit consumption with an option to pause further burst expansion pending approval.

Ben / Karthik: a few technical asks for the contract addendum — can we define a preemption flag per model (true/false) and an ordered priority list (string list) that the infra will honor? Also need to confirm the max scale-up rate (suggested: 8 additional GPUs per 30s) to avoid noisy neighbor events.

Marissa Cole
Principal Products (Operations) | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: GPU slab sizing + burst playbook — CrownCipher Dedicated

Olivia / Aaron — thanks for the speedy feedback and for the prioritization guidance. Summary of the agreed pilot terms and next actions below (I'll attach an updated runbook and a redline of the addendum tomorrow):

- Dayparting: shoulder slab will be scheduleable by UTC windows; we'll use the Arlington region pool so you can shift to 02:00–06:00 UTC for the event.
- Pool model: baseline + shoulder will be non-preemptible and guaranteed. Ephemeral preemptible pool limited to batch jobs only.
- Autoscale & scale rate: max scale-up rate set to 8 GPUs / 30s; scale-down with 10-min cool-down after sustained sub-30% utilization for 5m.
- Failover: primary fallback is to the hosted-compatible smaller model (variant-alpha) with expected failover time ~45–75s. If variant-alpha fails to meet your SLOs, we will engage the throttled-response policy for non-critical paths.
- Credits & guardrails: initial burst-credit bucket = 400 GPU-hours for pilot month; automatic alert at 80% consumption and an opt-in pause flow.
- Escalation: one-hour oncall response SLA during event windows; senior ops oncall (Ben) will be primary.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the addendum redline and updated burst-runbook-draft.pdf tomorrow.
2) Olivia — confirm if we should enable the opt-in pause flow or lock automatic pause until your written approval.
3) Internal: Ben / Karthik please confirm the scale-rate and canary timings are implementable in infra.

Thanks all — looking forward to piloting this.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
